Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second essay. Rovman Powell leads his troops out to the middle and they are followed by the two Kiwi openers. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Devon Conway and Finn Allen to open the innings for New Zealand. West Indies are starting with spin in the form of Akeal Hosein. A slip in place. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the West Indies will be the happier of the two sides at the halfway mark, and they have momentum with them courtesy of the strong finish with the bat. On a surface that has been anything but true with variable bounce on offer, Rovman Powell will be confident enough that his bowlers can defend the total. New Zealand are right up against it in what is a virtual knockout game for them, and it will require a collective effort to get over the line. Back in a bit for the chase.

Sherfane Rutherford, the man of the moment, is up for a chat. He says that he is happy to get the opportunity and is pleased to contribute. Adds that playing the World Cup is a dream and he wants to contribute to the side. Shares that it was important to build small partnership and ends by mentioning that 149 is a great score on this wicket.

As for New Zealand, all the hard work got undone there towards the end, conceding 37 runs in the last couple of overs and that has resulted in a dramatic shift in momentum. As he has done so often, Trent Boult set things in motion with a wicket in his first over. New Zealand were able to build on that scalp as Tim Southee, who was brought into the side for this game, struck twice in his opening spell. Thereon, the Kiwis were able to exert pressure even after the Powerplay through Lockie Ferguson and James Neesham. Just as a partnership was threatening to flourish, Mitchell Santner helped them break the stand before Trent Boult got them a massive breakthrough, dismissing Andre Russell. However, the gamble to bowl their main bowlers out, leaving them to finish with Daryl Mitchell and Mitchell Santner proved to be too costly.

TAKE A BOW, SHERFANE RUTHERFORD! A remarkable rescue act from the southpaw has allowed the West Indies to recover from 76-7 to end up with 149. However, the start was far from ideal for the co-hosts, as they were rocked early with the departure of Johnson Charles. Nicholas Pooran threw his bat around but not for long and from there, West Indies kept losing wickets at regular intervals. Sherfane Rutherford and Akeal Hosein got together to steady the sinking ship and did a decent job. After Akeal fell, Andre Russell teed off from ball one but his stay was short-lived. Rutherford then joined hands with the lower order to provide the finishing kick. He was unfazed by the loss of wickets at the other end and turned the heat on in the last couple of overs. Rutherford took Daryl Mitchell and Mitchell Santner apart and through a blistering 39-ball 68 has helped West Indies reach 149.

FOUR! BANG! 18 runs off the over and Sherfane Rutherford finishes in style! Short and wide outside off. Sherfane Rutherford cuts it aerially into the gap between deep cover-point and the long-off fielder for a boundary. West Indies finish on a competitive score of 149 for 9.

It goes very high in the air but only as far as mid on where Rachin Ravindra takes a couple of steps back and takes it near his chest. A duck for Chase.
Commentary.Howout: c Rachin Ravindra b Lockie Ferguson
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Lockie Ferguson to Roston Chase, OUT! c Rachin Ravindra b Lockie Ferguson.

Commentary.Commentary: Honing in at the stumps, on a good length, Roston Chase stays rooted in his crease and drives it off the inner half of the bat to mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Lockie Ferguson to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Rushes the batter up straight away. Starts off on a hard length, on off, Brandon King hops back to play at it but gets rushed and gets an inside edge that rolls to backward square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Lockie Ferguson to Brandon King, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes full and straight, at the stumps, Roston Chase drives it but without much timing towards mid on. End of a successful over for Tim Southee and New Zealand.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Tim Southee to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Roston Chase walks in at 4.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! Expertly held by Devon Conway and Tim Southee finally gets his man! Southee stays over the wicket and goes into the wicket, outside off, Nicholas Pooran waits back in his crease and frees his arms to go through the off side aerially. The ball slices up in the air behind the wicket where Devon Conway turns around and keeps his eyes on the ball all the way through. The ball swirls to his left at the last moment but Conway adjusts well and settles under the skier. Nicholas Pooran is made to wait as the third umpire checks if the ball deflected off the wire of the Spider Cam. After a couple of replays, the third umpire is happy with it and Pooran will have to continue walking. Huge wicket for the New Zealand and this is just the start they would have hoped for in a crunch game.
Commentary.Howout: c Devon Conway b Tim Southee
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Tim Southee to Nicholas Pooran, OUT! c Devon Conway b Tim Southee.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Gets it through! Slower and fuller, outside off, Nicholas Pooran reaches out as he crouches and drags the shot to the right of mid on for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Tim Southee to Nicholas Pooran, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED! Daryl Mitchell shells it! Straight in and out but that was hit really hard. Bowls it on a short of a good length, on off, Nicholas Pooran hangs back and smacks it right off the middle of the bat straight to cover where Daryl Mitchell is in really tight. It comes at a good height to him but the ball does not stick and pops out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Tim Southee to Nicholas Pooran, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Flayed away! Southee drops it way too short and offers width as well, Nicholas Pooran frees his arms and slaps it over the in-field on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Tim Southee to Nicholas Pooran, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, on off. Pooran swings hard across the line but gets an inside edge that rolls toward the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Tim Southee to Nicholas Pooran, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched full, at the stumps. Pooran flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Trent Boult to Nicholas Pooran, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Serves it on a length, on middle and leg, Brandon King drills it down to mid on and gets to the other end quickly.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Trent Boult to Brandon King, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, outside off. Pooran hangs back and guides it to third man for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Trent Boult to Nicholas Pooran, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: This is much fuller but straying on the pads, Nicholas Pooran swats it up and over mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Trent Boult to Nicholas Pooran, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Slanting in, on a length, on middle and leg, Nicholas Pooran goes for a heave across the line but gets beaten on the inside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Trent Boult to Nicholas Pooran, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Not where he intended but Pooran will take it! Fuller and honing in at the stumps, Nicholas Pooran uses his feet and tries to turn it away on the leg side. Gets an outside edge that races down to deep third for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Trent Boult to Nicholas Pooran, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Lands it on a back of a length, on middle and leg, Brandon King misses out on the swipe and the ball brushes his thigh pad on the way to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Tim Southee to Brandon King, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: This is on a short of a good length, on off, Brandon King punches it down to mid off.

Commentary.Commentary: Dragged it on back onto the stumps nearly! Full and going across the batter, Nicholas Pooran goes for the drive but gets an inside edge that sneaks past the stumps and rolls behind square on the leg side for one.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling away, on a length, outside off, Nicholas Pooran lets it go through to the keeper.

Commentary.Commentary: Nicholas Pooran walks in at 3. Tim Southee will steam in from the other end for New Zealand.

OUT! DRAGGED ON! Angles it across the right-hander from over the wicket, on a length, outside off, Johnson Charles backs away as he moves to the leg side and shapes up to go down town. The ball keeps a bit low and catches the inside edge of the bat before crashing into the stumps. New Zealand strike early and it is Trent Boult who has so often do the job for the Kiwis.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Trent Boult to Johnson Charles, OUT! b Trent Boult.

Commentary.Commentary: Drags his length back and bowls it in the channel on off, Johnson Charles is happy to let that one go.

Commentary.Commentary: LEG BYE! Length delivery swings back into the pads. Brandon King plays all around it as the ball turns into the on side for a leg bye to start the game.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Trent Boult to Brandon King, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities. All set now. The players and umpires make their way to the middle. Brandon King and Johnson Charles will open for West Indies. It will be Trent Boult with the ball in hand for New Zealand. Let's play...
All in readiness now as the teams and match officials stride out for the National Anthems. We begin with the anthem of New Zealand followed by that of co-hosts, West Indies. Action is not far away.

PITCH REPORT - Simon Doull and Samuel Badree are near the deck. They reckon that some pockets are bigger with 65 metres and 67 metres square boundaries and a 74-metre hit straight down the ground. They further mention that there was torrential rainfall yesterday but the ground staff have done very well to get the ground in pristine shape. Share that it’s a recently re-laid surface and the average first innings score is 162. Reckon that there is patchiness on the surface and there might be variable bounce. They feel that West Indies will try to get around 180.

The skipper of the West Indies, Rovman Powell says that they would have bowled first as well. On not being able to practice due to the inclement weather, he says that he is okay with it as the guys in the team come on the back of a lot of cricket and rest is also important. Tells that they want to keep on improving in all 3 areas and there are a few boxes to be ticked in the batting department. Also says that they want to control their Powerplay bowling. Ends by informing that they are going with the same team as the last game.

Kane Williamson, the New Zealand skipper, says that they will have a bowl as there are a few unknowns in the surface. Adds that they haven’t had a lot of practice time with the weather around. Shares that it is about committing to their job and doing what they are good at. Ends by mentioning the three changes with James Neesham in for Michael Bracewell, Tim Southee in for Matt Henry, and Rachin Ravindra coming in for Mark Chapman.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Finn Allen, Devon Conway (WK), Kane Williamson (C), Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Rachin Ravindra (In for Mark Chapman), James Neesham (In for Michael Bracewell), Mitchell Santner, Tim Southee (In for Matt Henry), Lockie Ferguson, Trent Boult.

West Indies (Unchanged Playing XI) - Johnson Charles, Brandon King, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Roston Chase, Rovman Powell (C), Sherfane Rutherford, Andre Russell, Romario Shepherd, Akeal Hosein, Alzarri Joseph, Gudakesh Motie.
TOSS - The coin toss lands in the favour of New Zealand and they have opted to BOWL first.

As for the 2022 semi-finalists, New Zealand, they have had a rocky start and are teetering on the edge of elimination early in the tournament. After looking disjointed as a unit in their opening match, it's now or never for the Kiwis to get their act together. Kane Williamson will need to lead from the front, supported by Devon Conway and Daryl Mitchell in the batting lineup. The pace trio of Trent Boult, Matt Henry, and Lockie Ferguson will play crucial roles, alongside spinner Mitchell Santner, as New Zealand fight to stay in contention. Will this high-pressure situation bring out the best in the Kiwis? Let's find out as we await the toss and team news.

The West Indies have launched their quest for a third Men's T20 World Cup title with two commanding victories. Now, the real test awaits as they face critical matches against New Zealand and Afghanistan. Their bowling unit, yet to face a stern challenge, will depend on performances from Akeal Hosein, Gudakesh Motie, and Alzarri Joseph. In the batting lineup, success lies with players like Brandon King, Nicholas Pooran, Johnson Charles, and Rovman Powell, while the explosive Andre Russell is ready to make his mark with both bat and ball.

Hello and a warm welcome, everyone! The 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup has arrived in Trinidad, and what a mouthwatering prospect we have in front of us as the West Indies take on New Zealand at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy. A lot is riding on this game, more so for New Zealand with their tournament life on the line, and a defeat here will push them even closer to the exit door, whereas the West Indies can qualify for the Super 8 stage with a win.
